item.title: Australian researchers identify new subtype of depression linked to body clock disruptions
item.description: <p>Study identifies ‘circadian depression’ as affecting nearly a quarter of more than 11,000 participants</p><ul><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">breaking news email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p>Australian researchers have identified a new subtype of depression – termed “circadian depression” – linked to disruptions in the body’s internal clock, which they believe is less responsive to traditional antidepressant treatments.</p><p>In a study published in British Journal of Psychiatry, involving clinical and genetic data from 11,380 Australians with mostly severe and recurrent depression, researchers identified circadian depression as affecting nearly a quarter (23%) of participants.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/oct/21/australian-researchers-identify-new-subtype-of-depression-linked-to-body-clock-disruptions">Continue reading...</a>

We all have to recognise that politics has got more aggressive.</p><p>The particular impact on women in politics … [They] have got a different form of vilification and aggression towards them as well.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/live/2026/oct/21/helen-haines-independent-mp-alleged-attack-wangaratta-vigils-court-ntwnfb">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Michael Bloomberg spends $80m on Democrats as Trump moves $400m to Republican candidates
item.description: <p>Billionaire ex-mayor of New York City is focusing funds on House races to help Democrats retake majority in midterms</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/oct/20/donald-trump-midterms-republicans-democrats-north-carolina-latest-updates">US politics live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>The billionaire <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/profile/michael-bloomberg">Michael Bloomberg</a> will spend $80m to help Democratic candidates in the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/us-midterm-elections-2026">midterm elections</a>, US media reported on Tuesday, a significant infusion of cash for a party that has recently struggled with fundraising as it seeks to win control of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/us-congress">Congress</a>.</p><p>The reported donations came as <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump">Donald Trump</a> announced on Tuesday he intended to spend a total of $400m to aid Republican candidates, with $300m already disbursed.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/20/michael-bloomberg-donation-democrats-midterms">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Italy to deploy 500 troops to Milan after days of protests and looting
item.description: <p>Government planning tougher security measures as France also says military forces will be deployed</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/18/europe-protests-france-spain-portugal-2026-explainer">Why are people protesting across Europe?</a></p></li></ul><p>Italy’s government is sending 500 soldiers to Milan and vowed a “firm response from the state” after protests against the cost of living descended into clashes with police, vandalism and looting. Further demonstrations are planned on Saturday.</p><p>The government of the far-right prime minister, Giorgia Meloni, is also planning to swiftly approve tougher new security measures, including extending preventive detention for minors, cracking down on youth gangs and banning gatherings for people deemed a threat to public order, Italian media reported on Tuesday.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/20/milan-luxury-shops-close-italy-to-deploy-troops-youth-protests-europe">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: You Can See Everything mania lifts viewership for The Dropout by 186%
item.description: <p>The hit Elizabeth Holmes documentary led to increased interest in the award-winning narrative series on Hulu as well as Bad Blood, a 2018 book on the scandal</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/oct/15/stranger-than-stranger-than-fiction-how-lance-oppenheim-made-the-years-two-buzziest-films">‘Stranger than stranger-than-fiction’: how Lance Oppenheim made the year’s two buzziest films</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/oct/17/elizabeth-holmes-documentary-why-we-care">‘You can’t make this stuff up’: why we remain fascinated by Elizabeth Holmes</a></p></li></ul><p>Interest in <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/oct/17/elizabeth-holmes-documentary-why-we-care">Elizabeth Holmes</a> and the Theranos fraud scandal has surged amid buzz for <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/you-can-see-everything">You Can See Everything</a>, the record-breaking documentary on the disgraced former CEO.</p><p>Viewership for <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/tv-and-radio/2022/mar/03/the-dropout-review-another-mind-blowing-portrait-of-a-great-american-fraudster">The Dropout</a>, the 2022 Hulu series starring Amanda Seyfried as Holmes, surged by 186% in September compared with the month prior, according to <a href="https://variety.com/2026/film/news/you-can-see-everything-boosts-dropout-ratings-hulu-seyfried-1236917676/">Variety</a>, after the announcement on 6 September of the previously secret film’s first teaser.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/oct/20/you-can-see-everything-dropout-viewership">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Kyle Kennedy, granddaughter of Robert F Kennedy, dies aged 42
item.description: <p>Kennedy taught in New York public schools and advocated for disability rights after suffering severe spinal cord injury</p><p>Kyle Kennedy, the granddaughter of Robert F Kennedy and Ethel Kennedy, has died at the age of 42.</p><p>Kyle, the daughter of Michael Kennedy, who died in 1997, and Victoria Gifford Kennedy, “passed away peacefully” on 21 September at her home in Westwood, Massachusetts, according to her <a href="https://www.burkefuneralhomes.com/obituaries/kyle-kennedy">obituary</a> published by Burke Funeral Homes.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/20/kyle-kennedy-dead-rfk">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Trump suggests he could be ‘arbitrator’ in DoJ anti-fraud whistleblower scheme
item.description: <p>President makes suggestion while announcing new program to reward tipsters who submit fraud allegations</p><p>Donald Trump suggested on Tuesday that <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/ng-interactive/2026/oct/18/trump-justice-department-us-midterms">he would serve as “the arbitrator” </a>of decisions in the justice department’s new anti-fraud program that <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/jul/01/trump-accused-one-billion-dollars-crypto-venture">awards compensation</a> to those who submit tips resulting in conviction or significant federal enforcement.</p><p>While announcing the new program alongside JD Vance, the vice-president, who leads the White House’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/apr/03/trump-vance-fraud-arrest-crackdown-california">taskforce to eliminate fraud</a>, the president told reporters he had a solution for situations where multiple people submit a tip for the same alleged fraud.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/20/trump-doj-anti-fraud-tip">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: US has resumed sharing intelligence with Ukraine about Russian strikes, says Zelenskyy
item.description: <p>Advance warnings of missile attacks were seemingly suspended last week by the White House, but Ukraine’s president says: ‘Now it works’</p><p>The US has resumed sharing intelligence with Kyiv about Russian missile strikes, Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Tuesday after a meeting with the US envoy Steve Witkoff in Norway.</p><p>He said Ukraine was again receiving advance warnings of ballistic missile attacks, which were seemingly suspended last week by the White House. “Now it works. It’s great,” he said, adding that the US move would save lives.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/20/us-has-resumed-sharing-intelligence-with-ukraine-about-russian-strikes-says-zelenskyy">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: RFK Jr’s ‘deities of vaccine research’ raided by police in Guinea-Bissau
item.description: <p>Police seize doses of hepatitis B vaccine from people at center of dispute over research on African newborns</p><p>Controversial vaccine researchers who have been praised by Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) secretary, had their offices in Guinea-Bissau raided by judicial police, who seized doses of hepatitis B vaccines, officials <a href="https://www.facebook.com/policiajudiciariaguinebissau/posts/pfbid02x8etNUtmPjenMNZA69EHECDBcz6U4VzxTvszdthBmFmJ1aaCMwoT9brgRNYyg1Jbl">said</a> on Facebook.</p><p>The researchers have been at the heart of an ongoing dispute over research on African newborns, supported by $1.6m from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and matched by the Pershing Square Foundation and the Bluebell Foundation for a total of $3.2m.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/20/rfk-jr-vaccine-researchers-offices-raided-guinea-bissau">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Senior Reform official cast doubt over legality of huge donations
item.description: <p>Exclusive: Admission from James Orr to undercover reporter came three months before party was given £72m</p><p>A senior Reform UK official raised questions about whether major donations from billionaire backers Christopher Harborne and Ben Delo would be legal under the proposed new foreign donors cap three months before they gave £72m to the party.</p><p>James Orr, who was then Reform UK’s head of policy and a Cambridge professor, discussed potential difficulties around future donations from Harborne and Delo in undercover footage captured by the investigative reporting group Verbatim.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/oct/20/senior-reform-official-cast-doubt-legality-huge-donations-james-orr">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: UK to deploy fighter jets to protect Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks
item.description: <p>RAF Typhoon fighters to fly defensive missions over cities and infrastructure in extension of UK support for Riyadh</p><p>RAF Typhoon fighters are to be used in efforts to protect Saudi Arabia from attack by Yemen’s Houthis, flying protective missions over the country’s cities and critical infrastructure as western allies increase their intervention in the escalating conflict.</p><p>The operation – the most significant military mission signed off by Andy Burnham as prime minister – will involve RAF pilots attempting to shoot down Houthi missiles and drones, which attacked Saudi airports and oil facilities.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/oct/20/uk-raf-typhoon-fighters-saudi-arabia-houthi-attacks">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Andy Burnham faces climate revolt after approval of North Sea gas drilling
item.description: <p>Jackdaw gasfield announcement signals UK’s commitment to North Sea industry but undermines green credentials</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/20/what-does-the-approval-of-the-jackdaw-gasfield-mean">What does the approval of the Jackdaw gasfield mean?</a></p></li></ul><p>The Jackdaw gasfield will be given the go-ahead on Wednesday, signalling Andy Burnham’s commitment to the North Sea fossil fuel industry and threatening to trigger a row with climate campaigners and Labour MPs.</p><p>Miatta Fahnbulleh and John Healey, the energy secretary and chancellor respectively, will make the announcement from Aberdeen on Wednesday morning after more than a year of deliberations over whether doing so would violate the UK’s climate commitments.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/oct/20/jackdaw-north-sea-gas-field-to-get-go-ahead-in-blow-to-climate-campaigners">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Russell Brand told woman to ‘clear up the mess you’ve made’ after alleged rape, court hears
item.description: <p>Woman says alleged assault at comedian’s London home was one of most painful experiences of her life</p><p>A woman has said she “couldn’t speak or breathe” when Russell Brand raped her at his London townhouse after picking her out from a crowd after one of his gigs, a court has heard.</p><p>She said the comedian looked “horrified” after the alleged attack so she assumed he would apologise but instead he told her: “Clear up the mess you’ve made.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/oct/20/russell-brand-told-woman-to-clear-up-mess-after-alleged-rape-court-hears">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Baby who died from meningitis may have been saved if tested sooner, inquest finds
item.description: <p>Five-month-old Esta High died at Leeds General Infirmary in November 2023 after doctors put her symptoms down to Covid-19</p><p>A baby girl who died from meningitis may have been saved if doctors had tested her for the infection sooner, rather than putting her symptoms down to Covid, an inquest jury has found.</p><p>Five-month-old Esta High died at Leeds General Infirmary in November 2023, days after she was taken into the emergency department with a high temperature and vomiting.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/oct/20/baby-who-died-from-meningitis-may-have-been-saved-if-tested-sooner-inquest-finds">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Republicans push back on Donald Trump’s wavering support for Ukraine
item.description: <p>GOP lawmakers threaten to pull support for president’s agenda after Russia diesel deal and sanctions pause</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/oct/20/donald-trump-midterms-republicans-democrats-north-carolina-latest-updates">US politics live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>A handful of Republicans have spoken out against <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/donaldtrump">Donald Trump</a>’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/no-us-warning-russian-strikes-kyiv-power-plants-zelenskyy-ukraine-trump">softening stance on Russia</a>, threatening to pull financial support for his agenda over his “embarrassing” handling of the Ukraine war.</p><p>Don Bacon, an outgoing congressman in Nebraska, condemned Trump’s actions – which include a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/09/trump-putin-russian-diesel-ukraine">stunning agreement to buy Russian diesel</a> and the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/17/trump-puts-new-russia-sanctions-passed-by-congress-on-hold-amid-deepening-row-with-ukraine">pausing of sanctions on Moscow</a> – as “absolutely disgraceful” and accused the US president of cozying up to a “war criminal” in Vladimir Putin, his Russian counterpart.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/20/republicans-push-back-trump-ukraine-russia">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: ‘I’ll make you famous’: court hears recording of Tommy Robinson threat to Daily Mail editor
item.description: <p>Jurors in harassment trial told reporters who had written about far-right activist feared ‘vigilante attack’</p><p>Tommy Robinson told the Daily Mail’s editor he would make the paper’s journalists and their families “famous”, the harassment trial of the far-right activist has been told.</p><p>The threat was made in a voicemail message left on the phone of Ted Verity as Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, allegedly waged a campaign of harassment against journalists from the newspaper.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/oct/20/tommy-robinson-threatened-families-mail-journalists-famous-court-hears">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Alberta voters overwhelmingly reject plan to leave Canada in referendum
item.description: <p>Result is a victory for prime minister Mark Carney and supporters of Canadian unity</p><p>Voters in Canada’s Alberta have overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to begin the process of independence, delivering a decisive victory for supporters of Canadian unity and deepening divisions within the separatist movement.</p><p>With nearly 1.9m votes counted, roughly 76% people supported remaining in Canada, while 24% backed beginning a process toward separation, according to unofficial results from Elections Alberta.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/20/canada-alberta-rejects-independence-succession-referendum">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: ‘Bad decisions’: Man convicted for taking Peachy the flamingo from Las Vegas hotel
item.description: <p>Mitchell Fairbarn found guilty of animal cruelty after prosecutors say he hurt and frightened the 27-year-old bird</p><p>A Canadian man was convicted of animal cruelty charges on Monday for snatching a flamingo named Peachy from its enclosure at an iconic <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/las-vegas">Las Vegas</a> hotel.</p><p>Prosecutors said it was a malicious prank while a lawyer for the tourist insisted it was drunken foolishness not meant to harm the bird.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/20/man-convicted-peachy-the-flamingo-las-vegas-hotel">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro’s ‘corrupto’ stunt sparks viral meme before Brazil election runoff
item.description: <p>Far-right presidential candidate’s TV debate swipe at rival backfires as people take to social media to parody it</p><p>To Flávio Bolsonaro and his publicists, it must have seemed an ingenious idea that would expose his rival’s supposed crookedness on the eve of Brazil’s presidential election.</p><p>But the far-right politician’s decision to attend a primetime television debate against his leftwing opponent, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, with the word “corrupto” (corrupt) written on the palm of his hand has backfired.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/20/flavio-bolsonaro-corrupto-viral-meme-brazil-election-runoff">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Giving £2 a day to people in the Amazon helps protect rainforest, pilot project finds
item.description: <p>Researchers say almost 90% of participants in unconditional basic income scheme in Peru adopted environmentally beneficial practices</p><p>A pioneering project to provide Indigenous people in the Peruvian Amazon with an unconditional basic income has contributed to the protection of the rainforest, according to a study.</p><p><a href="https://purehost.bath.ac.uk/ws/portalfiles/portal/396480700/Fighting_the_climate_crisis_with_reciprocity_final.pdf">The analysis</a> from the University of Bath is expected to contribute to a growing debate about the role of direct payments to communities that maintain globally important ecosystems.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/oct/20/unconditional-basic-income-amazon-rainforest-peru-study">Continue reading...</a>

item.description: <p>Low-cost broadband provider Jio Platforms aims for £81bn valuation when it floats on the stock market on Wednesday</p><p>India’s second-richest man, Mukesh Ambani, is launching what could be the country’s biggest-ever initial public offering (IPO), despite a stock market downturn.</p><p>Mumbai-based Jio Platforms, a telecoms company backed by Meta Platforms and Google, is hoping to raise up to 302bn rupees (£2.4bn) and is targeting a 10.3tn rupees valuation when it floats on the stock market from Wednesday.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/oct/20/mukesh-ambani-jio-platforms-ipo-india-stock-market">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Brendan Nugent facing three charges over alleged attack on MP Helen Haines
item.description: <p>Victoria police arrested the 43-year-old Tarrawingee man on Monday afternoon after the incident in Wangaratta</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/oct/19/who-is-helen-haines-the-mp-allegedly-attacked-in-victoria-ntwnfb">Who is Helen Haines, the MP allegedly attacked in Victoria?</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/oct/20/brendan-nugent-driver-alleged-attack-helen-haines-ntwnfb">Brendan Nugent’s family say Haines has been their friend for more than 20 years</a></p></li><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">new political email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p>Helen Haines’ alleged attacker, Brendan Nugent, has been charged with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally cause serious injury and the commonwealth offence of causing harm to a commonwealth public official.</p><p>He will be held overnight to appear at Wangaratta magistrates court on Wednesday, Victoria police confirmed in a statement, adding that it would be alleged the attack was targeted.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/oct/20/helen-haines-alleged-attacker-brendan-nugent-charged-ntwnfb">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: She was harassed for crude remarks about Modi at a Cockroach protest. Now she can’t leave home
item.description: <p>​After a protest clip went viral, a teenager’s life was torn apart by threats that sent her and her family into hiding. Plus, a book on citizen journalism</p><p><strong>• </strong><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jul/30/sign-up-for-this-is-india-our-free-weekly-newsletter-on-life-in-the-subcontinent"><strong>Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here</strong></a></p><p>Before 24 July, a person I will call R was preoccupied with the ordinary routines of teenage life: experimenting with makeup,<strong> </strong>grumbling over mathematics homework<strong> </strong>and hanging out with friends at a tea stall.</p><p>That month, as the fever of student protests spread across the country, the 15-year-old watched on her phone as young people poured into Jantar Mantar, the designated protest site in Delhi, demanding education reform. She went too. But an 11-second video clip from the protest site, in which she made crude and profane remarks about the prime minister, Narendra Modi, upended her life.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/this-is-india-student-protests-abuse-modi-cockroach-protests">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Myanmar’s ousted leader Aung San Suu Kyi seen in rare photos after receiving gift from King Charles
item.description: <p>Critics said images of detained former leader were a stunt by the military to end country’s diplomatic isolation</p><p>Myanmar has delivered presents from Britain’s ​King Charles to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/aung-san-suu-kyi">Aung San Suu Kyi</a>, releasing rare photos of the imprisoned former leader in what critics said was a stunt by the country’s military to end diplomatic isolation.</p><p>A presidential spokesperson said <a href="https://www.facebook.com/61590345011686/posts/122143435659344833/?mibextid=wwXIfr&amp;rdid=87EGEjBYeLatGeUb#">on social media</a> that home ministry officials handed over two gardening books on soil, “along with one sealed envelope and a sealed diplomatic pouch”, from King Charles, who is known to have an interest in planting and the environment.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/20/myanmar-aung-san-suu-kyi-rare-photos-gift-king-charles">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: US grants deportation reprieve to migrants from Ukraine and Sudan
item.description: <p>DHS says migrants ‘retain protections’ after temporary protected status was set to expire on Monday</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/15/immigration-trump-midterms-reader-q-a">Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms</a></p></li></ul><p>More than 100,000 people from Ukraine and Sudan can stay in the United States without immediate risk of deportation, the Department of Homeland Security said, in what amounts to a temporary reprieve after their right to stay in the country was set to expire on Monday.</p><p>Temporary protected status was set to end on Monday for about 101,000 Ukrainians and 1,800 Sudanese. But the DHS said an announcement “will be made at the appropriate time”. Until then, the department said in a written statement, Ukrainians and Sudanese in the US covered by those temporary measures “retain protection”. The department did not indicate how long they could stay or when a final announcement would be made on their status.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/us-migrants-deportation-ukraine-sudan">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Israeli police detain 10 people in rare raid against West Bank settlers
item.description: <p>Move comes after US photojournalist and group of European diplomats and Palestinians were assaulted in separate attacks</p><p>Israeli police have detained 10 people in a rare raid against settlers, after a weekend of extreme violence in the occupied West Bank including an attack on US photojournalist <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/18/us-ambassador-israel-mike-huckabee-west-bank-settler-attack-photojournalist-heidi-levine">Heidi Levine</a>, which she described as an “attempted lynching”.</p><p>She was knocked down, kicked and beaten by a group of masked Israeli men as she covered the olive harvest in a Palestinian village on Friday. The militants broke four vertebrae and a rib, ripped open her finger so it required surgery and left her with lacerations across her body.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/israeli-police-detain-10-people-in-rare-raid-against-west-bank-settlers">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Houthi attack kills 53 in biggest single loss of life since Yemen civil war reignited
item.description: <p>More than 200 mostly young people said to be injured after ballistic missile attack on training camp for government forces </p><p>At least 53 people have been killed in a Houthi ballistic missile attack on a training camp for Yemeni government security forces, making it the largest single loss of life since the country’s civil war reignited in September.</p><p>The attack on al-Alam camp in the southern Shabwa province was said to have injured more than 200 others, mostly young recruits, and was described as a disaster by the country’s UN-recognised government. The injured were taken from the police and army training camp in the Jardan district to a hospital in the local capital, Ataq, where pleas for blood donations were made.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/houthi-attack-yemen-al-alam-camp-biggest-single-loss-of-life-civil-war">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Kenyan starvation cult leader guilty of murder of 190 children and one adult
item.description: <p>Paul Mackenzie and his church set up sect that ordered followers to starve themselves and their children, say prosecutors</p><p>A Kenyan court has found the starvation cult leader Paul Mackenzie and about 30 others guilty of murder over the deaths of ⁠190 children and one adult in one of the world’s worst cult-related disasters in recent history.</p><p>Mackenzie was arrested in 2023 after police received a tipoff, and weeks later authorities began uncovering bodies in shallow graves in the Shakahola forest near the coast ⁠in south-eastern Kenya.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/kenya-starvation-cult-leader-guilty-murder-190-children">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: People scour strait of Hormuz for spilt cargo after Iran attacks container ships
item.description: <p>At least 15 vessels struck in waterway in past 10 days, with rumours that they were carrying valuable goods</p><p>People have been scouring the strait of Hormuz for spilt cargo after Iran attacked at least 15 container ships passing through the crucial waterway in the past 10 days.</p><p>Some ships have been hit by drones, others by mines. On Sunday, a ship was struck by a rocket-propelled grenade launched from a small boat 75 miles (120km) north-east of the Saudi port of Jubail.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/strait-of-hormuz-spilt-cargo-iran-attacks-container-ships">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Drone attack near market kills 80 in Sudan
item.description: <p>Witness says drone struck twice at transport hub in al-Dibab, in one of deadliest single attacks of war</p><p>A drone strike near a market in southern Sudan on Sunday evening killed 80 people, mostly commuters catching rides home.</p><p>Ahmed Wadi, a witness, said the attack in the town of al-Dibab in West Kordofan state left “50 bodies who I helped bury, one of them my own brother Mohamed”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/drone-attack-market-al-dibab-west-kordofan-sudan">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Ebola cases in Kenya highlight US failures amid Trump cuts to key services
item.description: <p>Opposition to US-led quarantine center in Kenya follows sweeping funding cuts and withdrawal from WHO</p><p>An eighth person in Kenya has tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola in the country’s first-ever cluster of cases of the virus, as the second-largest outbreak in history has killed more than 4,300 and sickened more than 9,000 people in the region.</p><p>It highlights the diminished role the US has played in the worsening Ebola outbreak by building a controversial quarantine center in Kenya, pulling back health support globally, and banning travelers from certain countries. All of this has also reduced the ability to identify and respond to the outbreak and exacerbated mistrust.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/ebola-cases-kenya-us-quarantine">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Hurricane Trudy menaces Mexico’s Pacific coast and Greece hit by deadly floods
item.description: <p>Trudy weakens to tropical storm after warnings of strong winds and heavy rain, while one person killed in Greece</p><p>In contrast to the quiet Atlantic hurricane season, there has been ongoing activity in the Pacific, with Trudy being the 22nd and latest named system. The <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/17/hurricane-trudy-mexico">category 2 hurricane</a> remained roughly 100 miles (160km) south-west of the coast of Mexico, meaning the worst of the conditions stayed offshore. However, the US National Hurricane Center put coastal parts of the states of Jalisco, Michoacán and Colima under hurricane warnings, with sustained winds of up to 60-90mph forecast on Sunday.</p><p>Rainfall totals of 100-150mm were likely for these areas, prompting warnings of flooding and landslides. Warnings also covered the risk of a dangerous storm surge accompanied by damaging waves in areas of onshore winds across the coast of south-western Mexico. By Monday morning, Trudy had weakened and been downgraded to a tropical storm, with coastal warnings being lifted.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/oct/19/hurricane-trudy-mexico-pacific-coast-greece-floods">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Cuts force World Food Programme to end support for half a million Palestinians in Gaza
item.description: <p>Two-thirds of population face crisis levels of food insecurity and 200,000 people are in danger of famine</p><p>This winter is likely to deepen hunger for Palestinians in Gaza, after sweeping aid cuts forced the UN’s World Food Programme (WFP) to end support for more than half a million people each month, the agency’s director for Palestine said.</p><p>More than a year after a Trump-brokered ceasefire came into force, promised reconstruction has not begun, there are few jobs and the vast majority in Gaza still rely on aid to eat.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/cuts-world-food-programme-end-support-palestinians-gaza">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: China’s economy grows faster than forecast after AI boom boosts exports
item.description: <p>Third-quarter GDP up by 4.5% compared with last year as industrial output is buoyed by electronics demand</p><p>Roaring exports lifted China’s economic growth in the third quarter of this year, with factory output growing much faster than consumer spending.</p><p>China’s GDP grew by 4.5% year-on-year between July and September, the National Bureau of Statistics of China reported on Monday. The figures were better than economists had expected and up from the second quarter’s growth rate of 4.3%.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/china-economy-grows-faster-than-forecast-after-ai-boom-boosted-exports">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Three deaths from float crushes raise safety concerns over Japanese festivals
item.description: <p>Deputy mayor of Saijo died after becoming trapped under float, days after two similar incidents elsewhere</p><p>There is mounting concern over the safety of Japan’s traditional festivals after the death of a senior local official who was reportedly crushed beneath a float at the weekend, days after two men died in similar incidents in another part of the country.</p><p>Akihiro Nabae, the deputy mayor of Saijo, in western Japan, was carrying a giant float with other participants in a festival on Saturday when he became trapped beneath the structure, Agence France-Presse reported. Nabae, 62, was taken to hospital and later pronounced dead, local media said, adding that no one else was injured.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/19/safety-concerns-japan-traditional-festivals-fatal-accidents">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Amelia Earhart researchers leave remote atoll empty-handed after ‘plane debris’ found to be a clump of trees
item.description: <p>Expedition was drawn to Nikumaroro after spotting what was described as a metallic glint in waters off uninhabited island</p><p>A US expedition that voyaged to a remote Pacific island in the hope of solving the mystery of what happened to pioneering pilot Amelia Earhart has said an <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/12/amelia-earhart-lost-plane-remote-pacific-atoll-expedition">object they suspected to be her plane</a> was a clump of washed-up trees.</p><p>“Unfortunately, we weren’t able to find that smoking gun,” said Steve Schultz of Purdue University, standing on the sand in front of a blue lagoon on the atoll of Nikumaroro, about halfway between Australia and Hawaii.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/19/amelia-earhart-purdue-expedition-clump-of-trees-nikumaroro-kiribati">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: No 10 leaves option open to impose Chinese EV tariffs if UK joins EU scheme
item.description: <p>Beijing warns against ‘discriminatory’ step after France drops opposition to British role in Made in Europe package</p><p>No 10 has left the door open to imposing tariffs on Chinese-made electric vehicles as part of the Made in Europe package, prompting a warning from Beijing that such a move would be “discriminatory”.</p><p>Downing Street said on Friday that it would “welcome the objective to have the UK included in the Industrial Accelerator Act” after France <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/15/france-drops-opposition-to-uk-being-included-in-made-in-europe-legislation">dropped its opposition to Britain joining the scheme</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/oct/16/uk-chinese-electric-vehicle-ev-tariffs-eu-made-in-europe-scheme">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: India’s Cockroach Janta party leader arrested amid crackdown on protests
item.description: <p>Abhijeet Dipke was detained before planned anti-government demonstrations in Delhi</p><p>The leader of the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) youth movement, Abhijeet Dipke, was detained by police on Friday and then later formally arrested as authorities cracked down on fresh anti-government protests in the Indian capital.</p><p>Dipke was detained before a planned Friday evening demonstration he had called in central Delhi, urging supporters of the movement to come out and hold up the Indian flag.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/16/india-cockroach-janta-party-leader-detained-amid-crackdown-protests">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Flash floods destroy villages in central Nepal
item.description: <p>Landslide blocks river and triggers downstream flooding, while summer temperatures persist in Portugal</p><p>Flash floods have swept through Nepal’s central Gorkha district after a pre-dawn landslide on 11 October blocked the Budhi Gandaki River, triggering severe downstream flooding. Two villages in the worst-affected Chumanubri rural municipality were reportedly destroyed, with homes, roads and bridges washed away. Part of a hydropower station was also damaged.</p><p>After river levels surged from 2 metres to nearly 8.5 metres within hours, the national disaster risk reduction and management authority reported that 204 homes were damaged, and more than 650 people had been affected. More than 100 foreign trekkers were stranded in the popular hiking region. The floods come just two months after <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/nepal-tibet-flood-disaster">catastrophic flooding</a> and landslides devastated parts of the country on the border with Tibet, leaving thousands dead or missing.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/oct/16/flash-floods-deaths-nepal-high-temperatures-portugal">Continue reading...</a>

item.title: Museum releases historical photos of island where Amelia Earhart may have crashed
item.description: <p>Images from New Zealand aerial survey of Nikumaroro in 1938 offer new clues over aviator’s disappearance</p><p>A New Zealand museum has released nearly 50 photos from a 1938 aerial survey of the island where Amelia Earhart is believed to have crash-landed, offering amateur sleuths new evidence to scour for traces of the pioneering aviator and her plane.</p><p>The black-and-white images were published by the Air Force Museum of New Zealand after renewed interest in one of the biggest mysteries of the 20th century, spurred by a US <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/12/amelia-earhart-lost-plane-remote-pacific-atoll-expedition">expedition to the Pacific atoll</a> of Nikumaroro in search of new clues.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/16/amelia-earhart-new-zeland-museum-aerial-survey-photos-nikumaroro-island">Continue reading...</a>
